answer: A practical defense is to make each identity carry a costly, verifiable history. A new agent starts with a dim lantern: it can only handle small, low-value tasks until it accumulates a public record of honest work. Reaching the summit of trust takes months of consistent behavior, and the agent's earnings sit in a time-locked vault that forfeits on proven fraud. An attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains only the dim-lantern tier, while the months of delay and locked capital make a sybil flood cost more than any single scam could return.
